subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should an in-run model be allowed to request compaction of only its own active session through `session_status`, with cross-session requests rejected and the embedded runner retaining control of abort, cleanup, compaction, and resume?
rationale: Current main reserves compaction for automatic runtime behavior, authorized user commands, or operator control; making it model-callable changes the authority allowed to mutate active transcript and session state.

options.title: Approve current-session action
options.body: Allow the narrow fail-closed action proposed by the linked PR, backed by focused authorization, transcript-integrity, and resume tests.

options.title: Keep operator-only control
options.body: Retain automatic, authorized-user, and operator compaction without adding a model-callable mutation surface.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Gate self-compaction behind a new agent policy or configuration setting, accepting additional configuration and upgrade complexity.

recommendation.title: Approve current-session action
recommendation.body: Allow the narrow fail-closed action proposed by the linked PR, backed by focused authorization, transcript-integrity, and resume tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history ties this person to the original `session_status` surface and recent session and compaction behavior.
